start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the workflow for <what I want done>." wf reads the workflow definitions this converter wrote from the Workshop installed on this computer. You never run the converter by hand.
no_lists_because: It reads the workflow recipe files and kept definitions of the installed Workshop and writes definition files on this computer; no list of yours is read or written.
instructions: 1. wf refreshes its definitions when a call finds the Workshop's main has moved; nothing needs to be typed.
2. The converter runs from the installed Workshop tree (wf keeps no copy), and writes one definition file per recipe plus definitions-index.json beside them.
3. A recipe whose bytes are unchanged since the last conversion keeps its definition file; a code change converts every recipe again.

worked_examples.title: Refresh after one recipe changed
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:send-a-tour for a student named in my message
worked_examples.given: The installed Workshop holds 579 recipes; one of them, workflow:act-on-my-notice, changed its label since the last conversion.
worked_examples.hands_back: The converter converted 1 recipe and reused 572 (0.98 s), so workflow:send-a-tour runs from its definition file as it was.
